{"id":"mimid-1wgh.108","title":"mimid: parent-dependent rooms are parsed but not implemented, so no call room can be hosted","description":"Found 2026-11-23 (bead mimid-1wgh.37.106).

room-policy-04 §5 L542 names the call room: "A room can be both
fixed_membership and parent_dependent, for example, for room used for a
multi-media call of clients in a Group DM". mimid cannot host one.

WHAT MIMID DOES TODAY: it PARSES the field. limits.rs:150 checks the
`parent_room` URI against the URI limits, and hub/state.rs:246 and
agent.rs:5269 both set `parent_room: vec![]`. Nothing enforces or uses
it.

WHAT §5 REQUIRES and mimid does not do:
- a parent-dependent room's participants MUST be a strict subset of the
  parent's;
- a user removed from the parent is automatically removed from every
  parent-dependent room of that parent;
- a parent-dependent room is always hosted on the same hub as its
  parent;
- `parent_room` MUST be set when the flag is true, and zero-length
  otherwise.

The second one is the interesting one to implement: it is a cascade the
hub has to run on every removal from a parent room, which is new hub
behaviour rather than a validation rule.

AND IT CANNOT BE IMPLEMENTED AS WRITTEN for the obvious case, which is
our own open issue ietf-wg-mimi/mimi-room-policy#40: a call containing
everyone in the Group DM is not a STRICT subset of it, so the rule
forbids exactly the example the note gives. Implementing this means
choosing a reading, which per AGENTS.md is a decision bead citing the
section and the competing readings. The candidate readings are "strict"
as written (and the note's example is simply impossible), or "subset" as
#40 suggests.

So this bead is blocked on nothing technically, but its first step is
that decision, and #40 being answered upstream would settle it. Low
priority until calls matter.","status":"open","priority":3,"issue_type":"task","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-11-23T18:55:53.457020566Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-11-23T18:55:53.457020566Z","dependencies":[{"issue_id":"mimid-1wgh.108","depends_on_id":"mimid-1wgh","type":"parent-child","created_at":"2026-11-23T18:55:53.49079061Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","metadata":"{}"}]}
new_value: {"notes":"PROMOTED in importance 2026-11-23 by the keying analysis on mimid-96tt. Working out where a MIMI-backed call's media keys come from shows that room-policy §5's call room is not an incidental example: MLS key material is group-scoped, and mls-extensions §4.4's exported secret is computable by every group member, so a call keyed from a room's exporter is readable by every member of that room rather than only the participants. Making the call its own group is what makes entitlement structural. So parent-dependent rooms are the prerequisite for keyed calls, not a nice-to-have, and the strict-subset problem in our own ietf-wg-mimi/mimi-room-policy#40 blocks the commonest case -- a call with everyone in the Group DM."}

{"notes":"RAISED TO P1 2026-11-23. Mark: "getting the vtc part right well demo
well, and is the feature that normies will demand."

That reframes this bead. It was filed as a spec-conformance gap, became
a prerequisite for keyed calls when the keying was worked out
(mimid-96tt), and is now on the path to the thing a demo rests on. A
call cannot be given its own room until parent-dependent rooms work, and
the keying analysis says a call must have its own room or its media is
readable by everyone in the parent.

WHAT A DEMO ACTUALLY NEEDS, beyond this bead, so the chain is written
down rather than discovered:

1. Parent-dependent rooms (this bead), so a call has a group.
2. The §4.4 exporter. DONE 2026-11-23, bead mimid-1wgh.4.82: mimi-mls
   Member::safe_export_secret over OpenMLS, with tests showing two
   members derive the same secret and a Commit changes it.
3. A media_keys component id and the media_secret derivation
   (draft-atwood-mimi-calls §4.2, §4.3). Small once 1 exists.
4. Signalling: a session part carrying the endpoint, which mimid
   already converts both ways (project.rs, backend.rs), and the VTC
   capability on the agent's JMAP endpoint, which it does not serve yet.
5. A media stack. mimid should not build one. SFrame plus a WebRTC
   client or SFU, taking media_secret as its input keying material,
   which is exactly where draft-atwood-mimi-calls §4.3 stops.

TWO DIFFERENT DEMOS, worth separating because they need different work:

- "Calls work": what normal users demand, and it needs all five,
  including a media stack mimid does not own. The long pole is 5, not
  anything in MIMI.
- "Calls are keyed by the group": needs 1, 2, 3 and no media at all.
  Two agents in a call room showing the same derived secret, a member
  of the parent room showing a different one, and a removal from the
  call changing it in the same Commit. That demonstrates the property
  nobody else has, costs no media stack, and is the differentiator
  rather than the feature.

The second is reachable from here and is the one that makes the first
worth building. Suggest doing 1 and 3 next."}
